signals.title: Display name claims a brand the domain does not belong to
signals.explanation: The display name claims Apple, but the message was sent from xn--pple-43d.example, which is not one of Apple's known domains.
signals.advice: Treat the branding as decoration. Verify through the brand's own app or site.

signals.title: Sender domain uses punycode or mixes scripts
signals.explanation: xn--pple-43d.example is an internationalised domain that decodes to 'аpple.example', which mixes writing systems within the name.
signals.advice: Read the decoded form of the domain rather than the rendered one.

signals.title: Message-ID domain does not match the sender
signals.explanation: The Message-ID was generated at relay.example while the message claims to be from xn--pple-43d.example. This is normal for mail sent through a service provider, so it only matters alongside the other findings here.
signals.advice: Corroborating evidence only. Read it together with the sender findings.

signals.title: Date header is malformed or contradicts delivery
signals.explanation: The Date header says 2025-03-01T11:00:00+00:00 but the delivery chain timestamps the message at 2026-08-14T03:41:52+00:00, a difference of 530 day(s). The two should agree closely.
signals.advice: A forged Date is often used to bury a message in a mailbox or to fake urgency.

signals.title: Authentication results are absent
signals.explanation: No Authentication-Results, Received-SPF or DKIM-Signature header is present, so SPF, DKIM and DMARC cannot be evaluated from this message alone.
signals.advice: Weak on its own. Note it alongside identity findings.

signals.title: HTML attachment contains an external form or script
signals.explanation: The HTML attachment contains a <form>. The form submits to hxxp://collect[.]example/harvest. This is how a credential-harvest page is delivered without a link.
signals.advice: This is a credential-harvest page delivered as an attachment. Do not open it.

signals.title: Filename contains a right-to-left override
signals.explanation: The filename contains a Unicode direction override, which is used to make invoice.exe render as invoiceexe.png (or similar) in a file list.
signals.advice: The override is itself the finding. Read the sanitised filename in this report.
